recognize_zh: 單核球細胞質邊緣有一個小圓形、帶清楚透亮暈圈的酵母菌體，外觀與附近的血小板大小相近但有明確的細胞壁與暈圈，需要仔細篩檢才看得到的念珠菌（Candida）胞內酵母。
features: Monocyte with abundant grey-blue vacuolated cytoplasm and folded nucleus
Single small round intracytoplasmic yeast form with a central dot and clear refractile halo near the cell margin
Yeast approximately platelet-sized; nearby free platelets appear similar at low magnification
Adjacent neutrophils with fine granulation, without visible organisms
Background red cells with overlapping; no extracellular budding yeasts or pseudohyphae in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a monocyte containing a single small round intracytoplasmic yeast form with a well-defined wall and surrounding clear halo. Adjacent neutrophils do not contain visible organisms, and no extracellular budding yeasts or pseudohyphae are identified in this field. The organism is of similar size to nearby platelets, so careful review is needed to avoid overlooking it. Findings are consistent with fungemia with phagocytosed yeast; blood culture identified Candida.

ddx.vs: An overlying platelet has purple granular centre with pale hyalomere and no refractile wall or halo, and lies in a different focal plane.

Histoplasma usually appears as multiple tiny (2-4 um) uniform yeasts packed within monocytes/neutrophils with narrow-based budding, whereas Candida is larger and can form pseudohyphae; culture or antigen testing confirms.
Vacuoles are empty without a central stained body, and Dohle bodies are pale blue irregular patches lacking a defined wall.
Bacteria are much smaller and rod or coccal, while Cryptococcus has a thick capsule producing a wider clear halo and variable size.
